title: No first-class Rust crate-extraction facility (monolith → workspace-member crate)
wanted_capability:
A reusable way to extract a cohesive subsystem out of a monolithic crate into a new workspace-member crate, as a guarded/transactional operation. Concretely: (1) scaffold the new crate — create crates/<name>/Cargo.toml ([package] + inferred [dependencies]) and src/lib.rs, add <name> to the root [workspace].members, and add <name> = { path = "crates/<name>" } to each named consumer's [dependencies]; (2) move the chosen modules/items into it with visibility bumped to pub at the new crate boundary; (3) crate-aware path rewrite — rewrite `crate::<seg>` / `use crate::<seg>` references in the origin crate to `<new_crate>::<seg>` (with use-tree splitting), and rewrite references from the extracted code back into the origin to `<origin_crate>::...`; (4) DAG guard — verify the extraction keeps the workspace dependency graph acyclic (this repo's contract-bottom invariant: implementation crates point down, never sideways/up); (5) validate via cargo check --workspace + rust_compile_fix_round with rollback across all writes. Ideal shape is a compound bbox_refactor_run macro `extract_rust_crate`, directly analogous to the existing `migrate_rust_mods_to_lib` macro but one level out (package→new-package instead of bin→lib), optionally fronted by a refactor atom for autonomous repeat use.</wanted_capability>
<parameter name="missing_primitive">A `extract_rust_crate` compound plan/macro (bbox_refactor_run) plus its three missing sub-primitives: a workspace-crate scaffolder (Cargo.toml + lib.rs + members + consumer dep-edge wiring), a crate-aware path rewriter (`crate::`/`use crate::` ↔ `<crate>::` with use-tree splitting, generalizing rewrite_rust_bin_crate_paths beyond the bin→lib case), and a workspace-DAG acyclicity check.</missing_primitive>
<parameter name="fallback_used">Hand-compose the sequence from existing within-crate primitives: write_file + multiple ensure_toml_table for scaffolding and dep wiring; rust_top_level_dependency_analysis to find the seam; extract_rust_items_to_submodule / move_rust_items_with_local_deps to move the cluster; migrate_rust_mods_to_lib / rewrite_rust_bin_crate_paths / move_rust_items_with_callers approximate the path rewrite (simple-name-segment match only, not crate-path aware, no use-tree splitting — leftovers need manual cleanup); rewrite_rust_*_visibility for the pub bump; bbox_refactor_run with cargo gates + rust_compile_fix_round to converge. No DAG cycle guard exists; relies on cargo check failing.</fallback_used>

notes:
extract_rust_crate facility need: peel cohesive subsystems off the root `blackbox` crate (the release-build serial-frontend pole) into workspace crates. Facility = the migrate_rust_mods_to_lib transactional shape generalized: scaffolder + crate-aware path rewriter + workspace-DAG acyclicity guard + the trap automations below. STILL UNBUILT — the campaign below was done manually/via dispatched bros; the gap stands until the tooling exists.

CAMPAIGN OF RECORD — code-intelligence cluster split. STATUS: COMPLETE (stages 0-5 merged to beta). Root crate 277.7k -> 161.2k LOC (-42%, -116k off the serial frontend). Extracted crates (parallel-compilable): bbox-vectors(3k), bbox-corpus-core(2k: entity_ref/git/edit-DTOs/Language/LspConfig/ProjectRecord), bbox-chunker(1.3k), bbox-lsp(1.2k), bbox-refactor(91.6k), bbox-code-nav(5k syntax-nav lane; indexed lane stayed root behind a facade), bbox-macros(15k). DAG: corpus-core <- chunker, lsp <- refactor <- code-nav <- macros. Follow-up tidy (not done, not a frontend-time win): the 10 tree-sitter grammar crates are now unused by root and can be dropped from root Cargo.toml (only bbox-chunker/bbox-refactor use them). Stages 2-5 executed by brodex gpt-5.5 bros in isolated worktrees, each independently re-validated + ff-merged by the orchestrator.

TRAP CATALOG (what the facility must automate — every item bit at least once across the 7 extractions):
1. DEP ENUMERATION (recurred in EVERY stage — the #1 trap): scan inline-qualified `<crate>::` paths (NOT just `use` lines), route test-only deps to [dev-dependencies], AND grep the crate's OWN PACKAGE NAME (here `blackbox::`, because src/lib.rs has `extern crate self as blackbox;`) — a `crate::`-only scan misses upward edges written via the package name (git->blackbox::config; lsp->blackbox::{config::LspConfig,util::test_env_lock}) AND misses inline deps like chrono/tracing/dirs (macros) and serde (lsp). The compiler eventually names them, but the scaffolder should pre-compute the complete set.
2. UPWARD-EDGE INVERSION: a would-be-foundation module reaching up into root config/state -> invert via a startup-injected OnceLock (child set_X() pub; root calls once after load; env/default fallback preserves behavior). Used for git notes namespace.
3. CROSS-CRATE DERIVE-VERSION ALIGNMENT: a moved type deriving e.g. schemars::JsonSchema may need a DIFFERENT version of the derive crate than root's direct dep (corpus-core needed schemars 1.x via rmcp, not root's 0.8) — surfaces as a trait-version mismatch.
4. cfg(test) HELPERS don't cross crate boundaries: parent-tests-consumed helpers need #[cfg(any(test, feature="test-support"))] + parent dev-dep (vectors); a within-crate test env lock is better replaced by a crate-LOCAL static Mutex (lsp, refactor) since cross-crate tests are separate processes.
5. PATH-RELATIVE RESOURCES break on move: tests/code building paths from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR with a hard-coded module segment ("src/refactor/test_fixtures"), and include_str!("../...") relative paths, must be re-rooted to the new crate depth (refactor fixtures; macros include_str!).
6. cargo fmt MULTI-TENANT OVER-REACH: `cargo fmt` reformats unrelated peer files in a shared tree; restore them (scoped) before committing — only the extraction surface should change. (All 3 bro-executed stages hit + correctly handled this.)
7. RE-EXPORT ALIAS = default low-churn caller strategy: `use <child> as <oldmod>;` (or `pub use`) in root lib.rs makes all `crate::<oldmod>::*` resolve unchanged (0 churn across all inbound sites). When lowering a TYPE, leave `pub use <child>::Type;` in its old home.
8. SELECTIVE pub PROMOTION is auto-driven: cargo check forces exactly the cross-boundary symbols to pub — INCLUDING ones whose need only appears because a sibling ROOT module uses them across the new boundary (stage 3's check forced refactor::{parse_report,resolve_path} pub because root's still-in-place code_nav used them — so stage 4 had its precondition already met).
9. SELF-PATH REWRITE: absolute `crate::<oldmod>::sub::X` inside moved code -> `crate::sub::X`; re-export shims `pub(crate) use crate::<oldmod>::{...}` -> `pub(crate) use crate::{...}`.
10. ORPHAN RULE: move ALL inherent+trait impls of a moved type WITH the type.
11. SPLIT (not move) via a ROOT FACADE: when only PART of a module can leave (code_nav's index-free live lane moves; its tantivy/index-bound lane + dispatcher must stay root because they reach up into `index`), the root keeps a facade module: `pub use <child>::*;` + the retained root-side functions + a dispatcher that routes to either `<child>::live_fn` or the local `indexed_fn`. Consumers' `crate::<mod>::*` resolve for both moved and retained symbols unchanged. The child must NOT depend on root (cycle); the retained lane stays root-side. Hardest pattern; needs a clean function-level (not file-level) index/no-index boundary.
resolution_note: Shipped in commit c8ff47f (beta/blackbox-v2): `extract_rust_crate` bbox_refactor_run compound + the three sub-primitives the gap named — extract_rust_crate_scaffold (workspace-crate scaffolder: Cargo.toml with inferred/rebased deps, lib.rs, members merge, consumer dep wiring, sha-guarded file-tree moves, visibility-preserving mod→use alias swap), rewrite_rust_crate_paths (crate-aware path rewrite WITH use-tree splitting for mixed groups), rust_workspace_dag_check (path-dep acyclicity guard, dev-deps excluded per cargo semantics). Design deviation from the gap sketch: v1 uses the re-export-alias shape (origin `use <crate>::<m>;` keeps every crate::<m> call site working) instead of mass origin-path rewriting, and enforces a fail-closed leaf invariant (refuses non-leaf modules with file:line offenders) rather than attempting cross-module visibility bumps — matching the pattern validated by the bbox-packets and bbox-system-memory hand-peels. Validation pipeline included (cargo check --workspace + rust_compile_fix_round + rollback). Side fix: analysis-only plan kinds are now legal bbox_refactor_run steps (runner + apply previously rejected all edit-less plans). 7 tests incl. live end-to-end. Runbook: sm-refactor-rust. Atom front-end deliberately deferred.
